candidates.source_title: New home plan for historic farmhouse garden is blocked - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Plans to build a house on the grounds of a large historic farmhouse have been refused. Jonathan Mulroy applied to Rochdale Council for planning permission to build a four-bedroom home and car port at the rear of Standrings House, on the corner of Bagslate Moor Road and Greenview Drive, Norden. Grade-II listed Standrings House was built in 1791 and was originally a moorland farmstead. It was converted to a home in the 1930s. Planning permission has already been granted to create a new access in the boundary wall from Greenview Drive. Planning documents submitted by Paul Butler Associates, on behalf of Mark Bell Architects Ltd, stated: “The proposals involve the creating of a separate plot at the bottom of the garden, more specifically the proposed house would be built in the south-eastern corner with access from Greenview Drive. “The proposed gate application would integrate into the character of the existing house and materials in order to create a secondary access for maintenance to the substantial rear garden. “The gates would be very much in keeping with the existing main gates and blend into the local character of the wall and surroundings. candidates.source_summary: A court has ruled that Rochdale Council did not act unfairly in its decision not to pass ownership of Hopwood Hall to one of its descendants.
candidates.source_title: Court rules in ownership row over Hopwood Hall - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A court has ruled that Rochdale Council did not act unfairly in its decision not to pass ownership of Hopwood Hall to one of its descendants. Today marked the end of a two-day trial in the High Court in Manchester after Hopwood DePree took legal action against the council which ended an exclusivity agreement to sell the historic Grade II-listed hall to him. Following the decision, Mr DePree said: “This is of course incredibly disappointing and a huge blow to our community, our supporters around the world, as well as the UK’s charitable heritage rescue groups in general. “However, please know that my team and I are already determining our legal options and next steps. “We will be watching closely to keep an eye on Rochdale Borough Council’s efforts to save Hopwood Hall for the community, and restore it to its former glory.” Mr DePree is a descendant of the Hopwood family which build the manor house in the 1420s. The family owned the hall and surrounding land — which is now Hopwood Hall College — until 1922. The house was sold 20 years later. It was occupied by a variety of temporary residents, including the de la Salle Brothers, who ran it as a Catholic teacher training college until the 1980s. It had fallen into disrepair and was bought by Rochdale Council, which still owns the Grade II-listed property. READ MORE:Rochdale Diversity Awards 2026 Finalists Announced

candidates.source_title: Man jailed for sexually assaulting woman and masturbating in front of her
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A sex offender who exposed himself to a woman on a train then masturbated in front of her has been jailed, following a British Transport Police (BTP) investigation. Nisan Fernando Kurukulasuriya, 39, and of Troutbeck Road, was sentenced to eight months' imprisonment at Manchester Crown Court on Tuesday 15 September. He pleaded guilty to Sexual Assault and Outraging Public Decency at a previous court hearing. He was also handed a 10-year Sexual Harm Prevention Order (SHPO) which will bar him from sitting next to any woman he doesn't know on public transport, and will be on the sex offenders register for 10 years. The court heard how, on Monday 20 April 2026, Kurukulasuriya was on a train from Stoke to Manchester when he sat next to a woman he didn't know who was on the phone. He then sexually assaulted her repeatedly, doing so again even after being pushed away by the woman. The woman then noticed that he had exposed himself and was masturbating in front of her. She shouted at Kurukulasuriya, who in response stood up and ran away to leave the train. The woman immediately got up to report the incident to staff. When the train arrived at Manchester Piccadilly, the woman went to speak to a member of railway staff. Kurukulasuriya meanwhile was stood only a few meters away, seemingly without a ticket that would let him through the gate line. The woman told a member of staff at the gateline that Kurukulasuriya had exposed himself to her, and the member of staff immediately contacted BTP.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A Hopwood Hall College student wore her wedding dress to collect her qualification just hours after getting married, as the Class of 2026 graduated at Rochdale Town Hall. Kelly Simpson, 44, joined graduates of all ages at the ceremony, where family and friends packed the Great Hall and cheered as students took to the stage. Kelly, who completed the Foundation Degree Early Years, arrived at the historic venue wearing a flowing white wedding dress beneath her black cap and gown. She said, “It felt very extravagant to graduate in my wedding dress – but why not? “I’ve had a great time studying at Hopwood and one of my lecturers even attended the wedding. “I just couldn’t resist combining two huge milestone moments into one big celebration!” The Higher Education Graduation and Awards Ceremony saw students collect certificates after completing higher education qualifications at the college. Emily Mills, who earned a BSc in Zoo Science and Wildlife Conservation, delivered this year’s graduates’ address.

candidates.source_summary: Four men have been arrested after police raids in Rochdale uncovered suspected illicit drugs, cash and electronic devices.
candidates.source_title: Rochdale Police Raids Uncover £1m of Suspected Illicit Drugs - Pharmacy Business
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A significant proportion of the haul consisted of prescription-type medication, alongside bodybuilding and weight-loss drugs The police uncovered a dedicated drugs storage facility for illegal drugs in Rochdale. Greater Manchester Police have arrested four people and seized an estimated £1 million worth of illicit drugs , allegedly supplied by an organised crime group, during raids across Rochdale. Officers from Serious Organised Crime Group (SOCG), supported by the Tactical Aid Unit (TAU), executed six warrants across Rochdale on Monday (28), following six months of investigation. The officers have uncovered what is suspected to be a dedicated drugs storage facility on Manchester Road, Rochdale. A significant proportion of the haul consisted of prescription-type medication, alongside bodybuilding and weight-loss drugs . The officers also discovered a list detailing more than 100 different types of drugs believed to have been supplied by the organised crime group, ranging across Class A, B and C drugs. The police carried out three arrests in Rochdale and one in Manchester.

candidates.source_summary: Peacocks Signs at Rochdale Riverside Retail & Leisure International
candidates.source_title: Peacocks Signs at Rochdale Riverside
candidates.source_body_excerpt: RivingtonHark, on behalf of Rochdale Borough Council, has secured British clothing retailer Peacocks on a long-term lease for a 10,181sq ft unit at Rochdale Riverside, taking the scheme to 92 per cent occupancy. The run of new lettings follows a 15.3 per cent year-on-year footfall increase at Rochdale Riverside, with almost 200,000 visiting during July, continuing an upward year-on-year trend throughout 2026. Following its opening in Spring 2020, Rochdale Riverside has delivered a dynamic mix of shopping, dining and leisure and is at the heart of the wider regeneration of Rochdale town centre. RivingtonHark has asset managed the centre on behalf of the council since 2023. The 200,000sq ft open-air scheme is anchored by a 50,000sq ft M&S store and a six-screen Reel Cinema and is home to leading national retailers including Next, H&M, Boots and JD Sports. Ollie Holland, Asset Manager for Rochdale Riverside at RivingtonHark, said: “The letting brings another nationally recognised retailer to Rochdale Riverside, activating a prominent, centrally located unit and further strengthening the diverse and growing fashion offer. The addition of Peacocks reflects robust demand for well situated space and continued confidence from national and regional occupiers in the long-term appeal of Rochdale Riverside. Rochdale Riverside is another example of how we work closely with local authorities like Rochdale Borough Council to deliver long-term value across town and city centre schemes. With footfall continuing to grow and further lettings in the pipeline we look forward to building on this continued momentum.”

In a nearby car park, a woman is getting dressed in a full-body fox get-up out of the back of a van. A man is belting anti-Brexit remixes of old pop songs through a megaphone at eight in the morning. These are just some of the sights that greeted attendees of the Labour Party Conference on their way into the Liverpool Experience Campus. Just as prominent as the frenetic energy of the conference itself – with attendees racing between venues and elbowing into the back of overflowing meeting rooms that quickly begin to smell like high school gyms – is the potpourri of protests happening outside it. Some of these have already had high-profile news coverage. On Sunday, Merseyside police arrested 82 protestors holding ‘I oppose genocide. I support Palestine Action’ signs “on suspicion of wearing/carrying an article supporting a proscribed organisation”. Detainees included 94-year-old human rights barrister Margaret Owen and Massive Attack’s singer Robert Del Naja. The arrests were criticised by Amnesty International as ‘a shameful attack on freedom of speech’. Monday saw a smaller but enduring showing of Palestine protestors at the tail end of the security queue. They did not appear to hold any signs related to Palestine Action. “We’re not going away. We’re here to send Andy Burnham a message,” said one of the activists. “The government might be making some of the right noises, but the fact is, the British government is still making us complicit. Burnham needs to act now.” At the foot of the Wheel of Liverpool, a persistent anti-Brexit campaigner has set up shop with a powerful pair of speakers, and lungs: Steve Bray. The blue-and-white-star clad character decamped from his usual position outside Westminster to treat sore-headed attendees to his EU-flavoured covers of ‘I will walk 500 miles (to rejoin the EU)’ and ‘You’ll Never Walk Alone’ – along with the European anthem. “Andy Burnham is going to kick open those doors to rejoin the EU,” Bray tells the LDRS with confidence. “His hands are currently tied by the manifesto. But he has a few years to get the message out to people, and I’m sure it will play a big role at the next election.” Mr Burnham is predicted to lay out plans to ‘edge the UK closer to the EU’ in his speech today, though he has previously said he ‘respects the decision made at the referendum’.

candidates.source_summary: Andy Burnham has delivered his speech to the Labour Party Conference, but did he do what most leaders do when their Party is facing a resurgence in the polls and could gain a new mandate to govern, if the polls are to be believed? Not really
candidates.source_title: Analysis: Did Andy Burnham's Speech bring anything new?
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Andy Burnham has delivered his speech to the Labour Party Conference, but did he do what most leaders do when their Party is facing a resurgence in the polls and could gain a new mandate to govern, if the polls are to be believed? Not really Burnham's speech focused on some main points: Triple Lock Reform, the Care System, and Energy. However, a lot of his speech was stuff we have already heard before from the Prime Minister: National Care Service, power to every UK postcode, and water - all things that Burnham either ran on or introduced following his election as Party Leader. But what does it all mean, and how will it affect you? National Care Service & Triple Lock Reform The big takeaway from this speech was the promise of the National Care Service, which centres on a care service that is free at the point of service, rather than the current Social Care provision. This means many families fork out hundreds, or even thousands, of pounds for private or council-supported care for their older relatives, and often complain about poor-quality services and poor working conditions. Burnham apologised for this, saying to the conference hall: "you are not invisible to me". He called the National Care Service essential to protecting the future of the NHS, becoming frustrated for Doctors and Nurses as he said, "we have let you down too...at risk of burnout...corridor care, your daily experience" We found out a little more about how he will fund this, with growing concerns over the last few days about a potential scrapping of the Triple Lock on State Pensions. Burnham tried to calm the waters, saying he would follow the manifesto commitment but would seek changes to the Triple Lock in 2030 by ensuring pensions rise by 2.5% while also not losing value against average earnings. This essentially downgrades the Triple Lock to a Double Lock, similar to a system that is used in Australia. However, the IFS has already said this alone would not pay for a National Care Service, which Burnham may not want to hear, as he pledged the scheme will be fully funded and won't need any additional borrowing. He also promised during his speech that Low-income Pensioners (pensioners who only have the state pension, or the state pension with a small private pension on top) will not pay tax in this Parliament. Burnham did not clarify where the limit was for those with a private pension, but the decision will largely be welcomed by those who fear the triple-lock increases will push them over the tax threshold.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Community equipment services provider Medequip has been awarded the contract to deliver the Community Equipment Loan Service (CELS) for Oldham, Rochdale, Stockport and Tameside (ORST). The contract has been awarded by a partnership of four local authorities, comprising Oldham, Rochdale, Stockport and Tameside councils, together with the NHS Greater Manchester Integrated Care Board (ICB). Community equipment services are a key part of integrated health and social care systems, helping to facilitate timely hospital discharge, support reablement and recovery, prevent avoidable hospital admissions and enable people to remain independent in their own homes and communities for longer. As part of the mobilisation of the new contract, Medequip will initially operate from the existing service depot in Dukinfield, ensuring continuity of service for residents and prescribing professionals. Medequip will then relocate to a purpose-built, spacious 32,450 square feet service centre depot within the Hollinwood Junction development. The modern, energy-efficient building has been designed with sustainability in mind and benefits from excellent transport and motorway connections, supporting efficient service delivery across all four boroughs. The new location will provide enhanced operational capacity and support Medequip’s continued focus on delivering responsive, high-quality services while maximising the collection, refurbishment and reuse of equipment through sustainable circular economy principles.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Luqmaan Ahmed (15/11/2001), of Heald Place, Rusholme, appeared at Manchester Crown Court earlier today, Monday 28 September 2026, and was sentenced for Encouragement of Terrorism contrary to Section 1 TACT 2006. Ahmed was sentenced to three and a half years in prison, with a one-year extended licence period. On release he will be the subject of a Serious Crime Prevention Order and part IV notification requirements under the Terrorism Act for ten years. In December 2022 Luqmaan Ahmed was sentenced to a 24-month Community Order having been convicted previously of encouraging terrorism and the dissemination of terrorist publications. He had originally been arrested in 2018 when aged 16 years old for encouraging others to join and fight for Hay’at Tahrir Al-Sham, a proscribed organisation affiliated to Al Qaida and for disseminating numerous pro-jihadist training videos via his Instagram and WhatsApp accounts. Officers from the Serious Organised Crime Group (SOCG), supported by the Tactical Aid Unit (TAU), executed six warrants across Rochdale this morning. Over the past six months, officers have worked to build a detailed intelligence picture, using surveillance, telecommunications data and a range of investigative enquiries to establish the scale of the suspected drugs network and identify those believed to be involved. That work led officers to several premises believed to be linked to the storage and distribution of illicit drugs on a significant commercial scale. During this morning’s warrants, officers uncovered what is suspected to be a dedicated drugs storage facility in Manchester Road, Rochdale. From the outside, the address appeared to be a residential property, but inside officers discovered vast quantities of suspected illicit drugs with an estimated value of more than £1 million. Officers also discovered a list detailing more than 100 different types of drugs believed to have been supplied by the organised crime group, ranging across Class A, B and C drugs. A significant proportion of the haul consisted of prescription-type medication, alongside bodybuilding and weight-loss drugs.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale Council has launched a “Stop Means Stop” campaign to remind drivers to stop for school crossing patrols. Councillor Dylan Williams, the council’s cabinet member for Highways and Facilities, launched the campaign at St Luke’s Primary School in Heywood. The council said it recorded 137 instances of drivers failing to stop outside schools over the past five years, including cases where a crossing patrol had already stepped into the road. “There have been multiple cases across the borough and across Greater Manchester with cars not stopping for the lollipop people,” Cllr Williams said. “This is obviously a real danger for schoolchildren across the borough. It’s really important that people stop.” The council is also asking drivers to keep yellow lines and school keep-clear markings free of parked vehicles. Cllr Williams said the increased parking patrols would take place without a fixed schedule. A crossing patrol worker at St Luke’s, identified as Chris, said vehicles parked on zigzag lines obstructed both his view and the view of passing drivers. Councillor Wolf said the building was not properly secured and criticised the property owners’ response. He said he was speaking to council officers about enforcement action and called for cameras at the site, including cameras capable of recording vehicle registration plates. He urged residents to report every incident to police so there would be an official record. People responding to his town centre post described further concerns. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Greater Manchester Police officers attended an address on Tweedale Street in Rochdale at approximately 4 p.m. on Monday, 25 May 2026, following reports of a concern for welfare. Officers discovering the 44-year-old woman deceased at the scene initiated immediate contact with ambulance services, though medical personnel could only confirm the victim’s death rather than undertake resuscitative measures. The initial incident classification reflected uncertainty regarding the cause of death, with responding officers treating the circumstances as potentially suspicious rather than immediately declaring murder investigation protocols. However, subsequent examination and preliminary forensic assessment rapidly escalated the investigation to full murder inquiry status. Detective senior investigating officers commenced immediate containment procedures, establishing crime scene security and preserving evidence for later forensic examination. Specialist teams from Greater Manchester Police’s Major Incident Team assumed investigative responsibilities, utilising established protocols for homicide inquiries. Kyle Howard, aged 25 years old and residing at the same Tweedale Street property where the victim was discovered, was arrested on suspicion of murder within hours of the police response. Howard’s presence at the address and circumstantial evidence established through immediate neighbourhood canvassing and witness interviews accelerated suspect identification significantly. By 3 June 2026, eight days following the initial discovery, Greater Manchester Police confirmed that Howard had been charged with murder and remanded in custody pending court proceedings. His appearance at Manchester Magistrates Court on 3 June 2026 formalised the charge, with the defendant remanded in custody pending further court appearances and trial preparation. Greater Manchester Police characterised the investigation as complete regarding the immediate arrest phase, though ongoing inquiries continued regarding potential additional circumstances or contributing factors surrounding the death. Greater Manchester Police’s Major Incident Team operates structured investigative frameworks encompassing witness identification, forensic evidence preservation, and secure evidence chain management. Following death notification to next of kin, supported by specialist family liaison officers, investigators establish timeline reconstructions, witness statement gathering, and preliminary forensic assessment protocols. Detective Chief Inspector Liz Hopkinson, of Greater Manchester Police’s Major Incident Team, told investigators that “this is a tragic set of circumstances where a woman has lost her life, and we have a team of dedicated officers working around the clock to establish what happened.” The characterisation reflects the emotional gravity of homicide investigations whilst emphasising systematic investigative commitment.

candidates.source_title: Vale of Lune battle back for victory at Rochdale on the opening day - lancasterguardian.co.uk
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Vale of Lune’s winning streak continued as they kicked off the new season with Saturday’s 32-28 victory at Rochdale, writes BARRY LEES. The first XV’s first meaningful encounter of the NW1 adventure had seen livewire flanker Sam Walton leave early for treatment to an eye injury. Reorganising ensued and the skill set of the crew on the bench began to kick in. Rochdale stepped up production and pressed into the Vale 22, where they powered over the tryline to open the scoring. They soon added a second to reinforce their intent as Alex Ryder came on to bolster Vale’s forward effort. From a sustained period of possession, Jordan Dorrington made the crucial break for Ben McGarvey to strike in the right corner. However, Mike Bradshaw infringed the rucking rules and was dispatched for a breather. It was time for Vale to dig deep and Eddie Abdelghafar led the backs’ charge, earning a chance for Jamie Mayall to slot over a penalty kick which left Vale six points behind the home team at the break, trailing 14-8. With Alex Briggs making a welcome return to first-team rugby after injury, a high clearance from the Vale fell to Rochdale’s nippy centre. They darted through the gaps to set up the next Rochdale try before more Vale changes saw Ben Gould come on for his debut in place of scrum-half Matty Kaye. A Rochdale foot in touch was flagged by the touch judge but overruled by the referee, with the resulting possession setting off a passing phase across the pitch for their fourth try of the afternoon. Sam Wallbank also transgressed the tackling laws, which meant he headed for the bench. With 17 points in it, a man down and 15 minutes remaining on the clock, it was no time for the faint-hearted. The Vale squad showed it is anything but that, starting with the flamboyant Jack Macfarlane pulling a try back and Mayall adding the garnish. Grafting together with increased energy, the Vale pack enabled prop Tadgh Butler to register his first try for the club. Three points behind and with the bit between their teeth, Vale rose in confidence and cancelled out all of Rochdale’s earlier advantages. The final word was delivered in the form of a relentless spell of Vale forward possession, well past 80 minutes, in the Rochdale 22. The ball was moved out to McGarvey, who then finished under the posts. Amidst the visiting crowd’s jubilation, Mayall - sporting a head bandage - kicked the conversion for Vale, whose first home fixture of the season comes against Leek RUFC on Saturday (3pm). Vale of Lune: Crompton, Verlaque, Butler, Sutcliffe, Procter, Walton, Ayrton, Wallbank, Kaye, Clifton, McGarvey, Mayall, Abdelghafar, Macfarlane, Dorrington. Replacements: Bradshaw, Taylor-Smith, Ryder, Briggs, Gould.

candidates.source_summary: Rochdale AFC Community Trust will hold its annual sleep out at the Crown Oil Arena on Friday 9 October 2026. The event has been renamed the Change Lives Sleep Out to raise funds for its Changing Lives programme.
candidates.source_title: Rochdale AFC Community Trust to hold Change Lives Sleep Out on 9 October
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale AFC Community Trust will hold its annual sleep out at the Crown Oil Arena on Friday 9 October 2026. The event has been renamed the Change Lives Sleep Out to raise funds for its Changing Lives programme. The Trust held its first Rochdale Sleep Out with Petrus on 29 August 2025. Together, the two organisations raised £7,875.52. The Trust used its share of the money to help establish Changing Lives, a programme run in partnership with Petrus Housing for people experiencing homelessness or living in supported accommodation. The Trust says Changing Lives has supported 33 people in its first eight months. It offers free football alongside wellbeing, personal development and employability activities. Its aim is to give participants a place to meet others, improve their physical and mental wellbeing, and find routes into volunteering, education or work. During those eight months, the programme has held 28 football and engagement sessions, five specialist workshops and four free haircut sessions. Participants have played two competitive football fixtures and attended two Rochdale AFC first-team matches. When the partnership was announced in December 2025, Scott Webster, the Trust’s deputy director, said it would give people “the chance to improve their health and well-being, develop a sense of community and belonging, and gain valuable skills for future progression.” This year’s sleep out invites individuals, families, businesses, schools and community groups to spend a night under the floodlights at the Crown Oil Arena. People can join on their own or as part of a group. Those unable to take part can donate. The Trust says the event is intended to support people affected by homelessness, rather than recreate their experience. Money raised will help continue Changing Lives and offer its activities to more people. People can sign up or donate through the event page .

candidates.source_summary: Ian Watson lauds Rochdale ‘courage’ after battling win at Fleetwood Cumnock Chronicle
candidates.source_title: Ian Watson lauds Rochdale ‘courage’ after battling win at Fleetwood - Cumnock Chronicle
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale manager Ian Watson believes his side showed their mettle in the 2-1 win at Fleetwood. Goals from Dajaune Brown and Aden Flint put Dale 2-0 up early on but they were forced into sterling rearguard action in the second half, especially after Tobi Adebayo-Rowling saw a second yellow card 21 minutes from time, with Mark Helm having reduced the deficit. Watson, who had come under fire during Dale’s slow start to the season, said: “That’s what we want to look like all the time. “I’m just really pleased we get to see what we’re actually working on, what we’re trying to look like, and how brave the boys were with the ball, how much courage they played with. “When they do that, it’s really hard for the opposition. I felt the first 20 was really pleasing, then I think we maybe played the scoreboard a little bit after that and self-preservation mode kicked in a little bit. “We got to half-time and I thought we regrouped, and started the second half really well. There’s so much I love about today’s performance, not just with the ball, but everything without the ball, and the heart and desire the boys showed as well. “I understand where the frustration comes from but my responsibility is to not listen to any noise, just focus and back myself as a coach, as a human as well. My mentality is strong and I believe in myself. But how amazing were the fans as well, they got us over the line.” Fleetwood manager Matt Lawlor cut a frustrated figure having seen his side start slowly and then fail to break Dale down for an equaliser.

candidates.source_title: Rochdale survive Fleetwood rally to secure victory - alloaadvertiser.com
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Ten-man Rochdale survived a Fleetwood onslaught to earn a 2-1 victory at Highbury. The visitors raced into a two-goal lead inside 14 minutes, Dajaune Brown netting with a first-time finish from Glenn Middleton’s cross in the eighth minute before Aden Flint doubled Dale’s advantage, coolly slotting home after Brown’s shot fell kindly into his path. Mark Helm hit back on the half-hour mark, pouncing on a loose ball in midfield and finishing neatly into the bottom corner. Fleetwood pushed hard for an equaliser, with Ched Evans’ shot deflected inches wide, Raffaele Cirino hitting the side-netting and Aaron Loupalo-Bi narrowly wide with a fierce low drive. The home side dominated the second half but Lewis McCann clearing the bar by inches was as close as they got. Dale’s task got even tougher on 69 minutes when Tobi Adebayo-Rowling received a second yellow card for a shirt pull. Goalkeeper Sam Waller then denied Evans and Flint got his head to Ronan Coughlan’s goalbound shot as valiant defending, and Fleetwood’s wayward finishing, saw Dale hold on for the win.

candidates.source_summary: A Middleton woman who stopped drinking in 2019 says writing horror stories has helped her explore her experiences of addiction and trauma.
candidates.source_title: Middleton writer says horror fiction has supported her recovery from alcohol
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A Middleton woman who stopped drinking in 2019 says writing horror stories has helped her explore her experiences of addiction and trauma. Alex Herod said she tried meetings, therapy, books and sober communities before she began writing fiction as part of her recovery. She has a diagnosis of complex PTSD and is now working on a creative writing PhD about the role horror writing plays in her own recovery. “Although I write fiction, most of my stories relate back to themes of addiction, trauma, mental health, transformation and recovery,” she said. “Writing horror has allowed me to go into very dark places and come out the other side. I can explore feelings of disgust and monstrousness - how I felt about myself when I was drinking, or how I felt others saw me - and do so in a way that is in my control.” Alex said being able to edit and rewrite a story gives her a way to express experiences she previously felt unable to discuss. She described the process as “making friends with my monsters”. “It helps me to process my experiences of addiction and trauma, and learn to accept and embrace the darker parts of myself so I don’t feel disconnected,” she said. Alex, who works at the University of Salford, is due to release her debut novel next year.
